- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.75) — model tends to be overly bullish.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.5) — model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — model overreacts, then corrects with a lagged dip.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to stay near recent highs, ignoring long-term trend decay.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overpredict early in the window (days 1–5) when sentiment is rising, then underpredict later (days 15–30) when sentiment stabilizes or turns neutral.
- Lagged correction: model often misses the peak of sentiment-driven rallies, forecasting a dip too early or too late.
